findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() silently returns null when the group has been deleted, changing the API contract
findings.body: The fix for the NPE changes `getSubGroupsCount()` to return `null` when the underlying group no longer exists in the database (`model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount()`). Previously it would throw an NPE (or IllegalStateException via other paths). `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` is declared to return `Long` and callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount()` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90) pass the result directly to `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long)`, and admin REST representations expose this as a numeric subgroup count. Returning null here means a concurrently-deleted group now yields a representation with a null subGroupCount instead of a consistent value or an explicit error, which can produce NPEs in downstream consumers that unbox the Long (e.g. JSON serialization paths or UI code doing arithmetic/comparison on the count) and silently masks the fact that the group was deleted mid-request. The correct behavior for a group that disappeared concurrently is to treat it as invalidated/not-found (consistent with `isUpdated()` and `getDelegateForUpdate()` which throw `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`), not to return null.

findings.title: Removal of groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement leaves an unused import and a dangling comment
findings.body: The diff deletes the private method `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` but the file still contains the comment `//From org.keycloak.admin.ui.rest.GroupsResource` on line 94 directly above `toRepresentation`, which referenced the removed code's origin, and the removal was not part of the NPE fix described in the PR. More importantly, the removed method referenced `org.keycloak.utils.StringUtil` (via `StringUtil.isBlank`); if that import existed it is now unused, and if any other code in the codebase called this private helper it would fail to compile — but since it was private, the real issue is that this unrelated deletion is bundled into a concurrency bugfix PR, making the change harder to review and revert. The deletion should either be moved to its own PR or, if kept, the dead comment on line 94 should be removed and the unused import (if present in the base version) cleaned up.

findings.title: Concurrency test has a race that can make it pass without ever exercising the concurrent read path
findings.body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` calling `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, but the main thread deletes all 100 groups and then sets `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) without joining the reader thread. If the deletes complete before the reader thread is scheduled (common on fast machines or under CI load), the reader thread may execute zero iterations, so the test asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty without ever having performed a concurrent read during deletion — a false pass that does not reproduce issue #40368. Additionally, the reader thread is never joined, so the assertion on line 157 can run while the reader is still mid-request, and any exception thrown after the assertion is silently lost (the thread dies with an uncaught exception). The test should `join()` the reader thread before asserting, and ideally ensure the reader has performed at least one iteration before starting deletes (e.g. a CountDownLatch or AtomicBoolean confirming first read completed) so the concurrent window is actually exercised.

findings.title: Concurrency test only exercises brief group listing, not the getSubGroupsCount path that was actually fixed
findings.body: The PR fixes an NPE in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (model/infinispan/.../GroupAdapter.java:272-276), which is invoked when `subGroupsCount=true` is requested on group hierarchy population (see `GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups` with `subGroupsCount` flag, services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:40-42). However, the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` — the `true` here is `briefRepresentation`, not `subGroupsCount`. The admin client `groups()` overload with a `briefRepresentation` boolean does not request subgroup counts, so the fixed code path (`getSubGroupsCount()` on a cached group whose DB row was concurrently deleted) is never executed by this test. The test would not have caught the original NPE. It should either call the endpoint that populates subGroupCount (e.g. the groups search with `subGroupsCount` parameter used by the admin console hierarchy endpoint) or directly fetch a group representation with subGroupCount while deletes are in flight.
